answer: Proof-of-Stake consensus acts as a digital river of capital, where an ember of computational trust is ignited by locking native tokens. By requiring collateral for participation, the cost of a Sybil attack scales linearly with the network value. A malicious agent attempting to carve a marble facade of fake identities faces prohibitively high capital expenditure, as creating redundant identities dilutes their influence rather than granting structural power over the decentralized ledger.
